The claim 'nothing was left unguarded / ownership is the lease, and always was' is hand-copied into three places with nothing checking the copies against each other: docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md:124, scripts/checklist_engine.py:95-97, tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py:25-27. It matters more here than usual because the claim is measurably false in the leaseless case (finding B1) -- one wrong sentence now has to be repaired in three files, and nothing will notice if only two are.

The predicate that had degenerated to returning None on every path was deleted rather than kept as a seam, and ORIGIN_EXEMPT_VERBS -- flagged as having no production consumer by three separate g1-era reviewers of #315 -- went with it. worktree_from_spine_path is left in place unwired and stated plainly as such: it is g1's shipped, tested derivation with a consumer named (g5), not a hook invented here.

78 lines of executable code were replaced by 14 lines of tombstone comment in checklist_engine.py, and the vacated position before dispatch() now carries an 11-line comment explaining that nothing is there. Some of this is earned -- a deletion this load-bearing should say why it happened, and the repo asks for exactly that. But the tombstone also carries the assertion 'Nothing was left unguarded by that removal', which is prose asserting a behavioural property that measurement contradicts (finding B1). CREW_CONTEXT 'Assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it' is precisely the rule this trips: the comment is doing work a test should do, and it is wrong.
